findings.claim: The script relies on every sh it meets treating dirname -- and basename -- as end of options; only dash with GNU coreutils was checked. If an implementation printed --, $general at line 83 would point to the wrong rules file and every kind rule would silently disappear. POSIX specifies --, so the risk is low but unproved.
The widened pattern accepts only lowercase suffixes, missing uppercase or dotted forms, and can match prose like L2-cache or S5-based as false positives; not reachable in current files.
The -- lint skips only lines starting with #; a trailing comment or message string naming dirname or basename fails it falsely, and a split or variable-built call is not seen.
